criteria.rationale: Checked L1, D1 and D2 against the code. Verified: the runtime directory is created exclusively, the claim is exclusive, and a failed claim removes only the directory this continuation took. L1's two guards fail toward refusing or recording. D2 accepts, as a recorded decision, that a continued session works in a moved directory. L1 no longer covers the untested claim-conflict return, reported in N7.
Lost take and lost claim are exercised by the new race tests, which also pass here; no directory sharing or re-run of a recorded continuation was found. The bounded uncancellable wait is N8.
Resume and handoff now answer a recorded continuation under the same rules as their plans; the stale spec sentence is N9.
Mismatched continuations return actionable refusals and a cancelled take returns the context error; the remaining planning wait is N8.
The CLI consumers already handle plan.Existing and PendingContinuation; signatures changed only inside package pose.
A moved checkout is recorded in safety.limitations and the thread reason names the held path.
Examined the CLI resume and handoff answers and the record fields: no schema change, and the new outcomes follow the existing plan refusals stated in D1.
Read the continuation paths and ran the focused tests; no behavioral defect beyond N8 was established.

No structural deltas were observed, so there is nothing to map. D1 addresses the cause of the wrong-kind result under R1 by applying the plans' rules after a lost race, and D2 addresses R3 by keeping the reserved attempt usable and recording the move.
Compared the added manual sentence in both locales and the embedded copies with the fallback code; they match. The inconsistency inside the spec is N9.
Examined the refusal and reason texts: they name the run that continued or the held path, and a cancelled take no longer advises removing a directory.
The subject's files are those the spec lists, including the new race test; nothing outside R1 to R6 was found in them. The undelivered part of R6 is N7.
Examined directory derivation, exclusive creation, removal on a lost claim and the test hooks: the hooks are unexported no-ops in production, and no new input crosses a trust boundary.

One small helper and two unexported hooks, following the package's existing hook pattern, are a small way to share the kind rule and make the races testable. Parallel tests in the package would invalidate the global hooks; a search found no t.Parallel there.

findings.action: Remainder of R1-N2. R6 is still traced satisfied but half of it is missing: no test resumes end to end a run with a recorded random runtime name (only the unit naming test), and none reaches the handoff plan's pending branches (delegation_handoff.go:331-337 and 353-356 uncovered); Known gaps admits both. L1 was also narrowed to two guards, yet the claim-conflict return of the winner's record that it used to accept still has no covering test (review_dispatch.go:782-784), as do the replan refusal (777-781) and the plan-level recorded returns and kind rules (review_run_continuity.go:440-448, delegation_handoff.go:357-364, wiring at review_dispatch.go:2241-2243).

Remainder of R1-N3. The take path now returns the context error, but the waits reached through replanContinuation still use context.Background() (also delegation_handoff.go:352), so a cancelled dispatch is not honoured there for up to about two seconds. The new ctx.Err return (review_dispatch.go:2246-2248) is uncovered by the focused tests.

API/contract changes still says a resume or handoff that meets another's recorded continuation returns that record, which contradicts decision D1 and the code: a continuation of another kind or agent is refused.
